notes.text:
1. AXES, REGIONS, METADATA, PROJECTIONS, AND GENERATED PSF
A TCZYX sample is cropped, reduced to one time point, split by channel, and inspected through spatial metadata and projection operations.

2. INTENSITY AND FILTERING
A small ZYX fluorescence volume drives an intensity-adjustment chain plus parallel smoothing, background, edge, and detail branches.

3. CHANNELS, RGB, THRESHOLDS, AND IMAGE MATH
Two registered fluorescence channels feed composites, arithmetic, logical masks, and a multichannel histogram; a compact bimodal phantom keeps the Minimum-threshold demonstration deterministic.

4. MORPHOLOGY, OBJECT SEPARATION, LABELS, AND TABLES
A thresholded 3D fluorescence channel is cleaned and separated, then measured through object, intensity, mesh, and table-summary paths.

5. COLOCALIZATION AND SPATIAL ASSOCIATION
The same two channels and ROI mask are reused across unmasked, masked, voxel, object, overlap, nearest-distance, and event-localization views.

6. SKELETON QC AND NETWORK MEASUREMENTS
A sparse 3D network is thresholded and skeletonized before parallel topology, labeling, pruning, overlay, graph-table, and summary outputs.

7. PSF PREPARATION AND DECONVOLUTION
A measured 3D PSF is prepared for Richardson-Lucy restoration, while the metadata-derived Born-Wolf PSF drives the TV-regularized variant.
